title: OKR Commitment Ledger and Cross-Team Execution Slate
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Company-level OKRs at Redwood are well-intentioned but often become vague wishes when translated into team roadmaps; cross-team dependencies drift, and execution ambiguity causes misaligned scope and missed outcomes. Goal: Create an "OKR Commitment Ledger" plus an "Execution Slate" pattern that turns company-level objectives into explicit, timeboxed initiative contracts with measurable acceptance criteria, owners, capacity commitments, and escalation paths. Deliverables: 1) OKR Commitment Ledger template (spreadsheet + Confluence) that records outcome statement, leading metrics, committed capacity (FTE / dev-weeks), acceptance tests (quality/regression prompts + observability KPIs), primary/secondary owners, decision rights, and fallback model variants. 2) Execution Slate — a canonical quarterly view that lists committed initiatives, expected milestones, unblockers, and a risk score. 3) Prioritization rubric for cross-team arbitration (cost, latency risk, regulatory exposure, customer impact, strategic weight). 4) Lightweight contractual artifact (one-pager) that teams sign off on during cycle planning and that ties directly to release gating and Console signals for measurement. 5) Rollout & escalation runbook: when SLAs/metrics drift, automated gating and manual escalation steps. Success criteria: clear owner for every company-level KR, <10% scope churn across quarter for committed initiatives, and integrated observability so Console dashboards reflect OKR KRs and alert owners automatically.

implementation_notes: Ledger fields: objective_id, KR statement, owner, secondary_owner, committed_dev_weeks, acceptance_tests (list of dashboard queries and eval prompts), measurement_dashboard_link, rollback_criteria, decision_rights, release_link
Slate view: canonical CSV export used by Release Managers to generate release gating configs; integrates with Console via a small webhook to tag dashboards with OKR IDs.
Prioritization rubric: numeric weights (strategic:30, customer_impact:25, risk:20, cost:15, org_readiness:10); final score drives arbitration during planning forum.
Sign-off flow: PM author -> eng lead -> design -> security -> exec sponsor. Sign-off recorded in ledger as timestamp + git-style commit hash for auditability.
Fallbacks: For infra-driven KRs, define compatible model variants (smaller quantized models) to enable graceful degradation without missing high-level KR metrics.
